parts:
Hi all,

First, sorry to Mike as I sent a separate message to him, but then realized I had a few more questions so I figured here was the best place in case someone else can help (so sorry for the double message).

1) I see that changing pct_wet also impacts the activity state.  How does the model do this?  Is there a threshold for water loss I am missing that can be changed? I did not see how or if pct_wet impacted activity state until I ran the model only changing pct_wet for 10 of my sites and calculated annual activity time and there was a difference.  However, I did not see anything about how this would be done in the ectotherm tutorial.  So how is that done and can the user change how it is incorporated (either in the function or by changing the code for the function itself)?

2) I am using the formula to calculate Pwet from chapter 11 of Behavior of Lizards (Hydroregulation and Climate Change).  The formula is Pwet = 1/(hd*R+(Pr/Sc)^2/3,  Where hd is the mass transfer coefficent (m/s), R is skin resistance in s/m, Pr is the dimensionless Prandtl number, and Sc is the dimensionless Schmidt number.  The values I am getting are around 0.6-0.8 when I use that formula (I am working with amphibians).  My question is, using that formula should I be getting a value between 0-100?  or are the values between 0-1?  Either way, in NicheMapR when entering pct_wet is that in percent or decimal percent? Based on the notes, it seems like it would be percent values between 0-100.  However, given I am working with amphibians a value of 0.8% would not make sense, so I want to be sure I am doing this correctly. 

3) A bit more straightforward, but for pct_mouth, assuming I am working with an organism that would not pant would it make sense to just set that to zero?

4) Are the cutaneous water loss rates only calculated when the organism is active?  Assuming they are rehydrating when not active?

If anyone knows, any help would be appreciated, thanks!

PS

I don't know enough about GitHub to suggest a change, but in the help file for WETAIR "denair Hourly predictions of the soil moisture under the maximum specified shade".  I am guessing that is a mistake and should be air density.

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Pct_wet Questions
parts:
Dear Vincent,

Here are some answers:

1) If you are running the DEB model, then there's a parameter described in the help for the ectotherm model as follows:
  

  • pct_H_R = 15, Minimum tolerated dehydration (% of wet mass) - prohibits foraging if greater than this

   But, if you aren't running the DEB model, then dehydration is not being cumulated and the only way activity would be affected is through the cooling influence on body temperature.

2) The function 'get_p_wet' in the package (is that what you're using?) is to get the proportion of the total surface area wet as indicated in the help, so 0.8, i.e. 80%, sounds right for an amphibian. You do have to make it a % for sending into the ectotherm model.

3) Yes just set pct_mouth to zero.

4) Cutaneous water loss is always calculated, but if you make it 100% humid in the retreat then they won't be losing water.

Good catch on the description of 'denair' - I'll fix that.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Pct_wet Questions
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Hard to tell without seeing the code you're running, but I suggest you start playing with the default model for the Eastern Water Skink and have a read through all the parameters relating to water in the help for the ectotherm model, and also have a close read of the Ecol Monog paper from 2018 on sleepy lizards.

One parameter you might be overlooking is 'raindrink' which by default is zero which means only 0 mm of rain needs to fall on a day for rehydration to occur. Try the script below with raindrink set to 0 vs. e.g. 1 (i.e. 1 mm rain) and you'll see some consequences on the growth trajectory and water balance - but I've made it quite leaky for a lizard (2.5% wet):

micro <- micro_global(loc = c(146.77, -19.29), timeinterval = 365, nyear = 1)
ecto <- ectotherm(DEB = 1, pct_wet = 2.5, raindrink = 1)
debout<-as.data.frame(ecto$debout) # DEB model outputs
plot(debout$WETMASS, type = 'l')
plot(debout$PCT_DESIC, type = 'l')

And if you're turning on the DEB model, it won't use Ww_g as it is computing the body mass, and by default starts as an egg so the wet mass in the output will be that of a freshly laid egg.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Pct_wet Questions
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I forgot to say that you can simply overwrite the soil humidity before it goes into the ectotherm model if you want to make it different from what is calculated. Tracy 1976 included equations for computing rehydration from soil - it will depend on soil water potential which is computed by the microclimate model.

Re the DEB model - yes L.p is structural length which will be much smaller than actual length. The ultimate physical length could be including the tail or not - should all be detailed in the mydata file. But it is possible that there are issues with the entry. Probably worth diving into some DEB literature to help you understand what you're seeing.

All the best,
Mike
